cve_summary: The bio_map_user_iov and bio_unmap_user functions in block/bio.c in the Linux kernel before 4.13.8 do unbalanced refcounting when a SCSI I/O vector has small consecutive buffers belonging to the same page. The bio_add_pc_page function merges them into one, but the page reference is never dropped. This causes a memory leak and possible system lockup (exploitable against the host OS by a guest OS user, if a SCSI disk is passed through to a virtual machine) due to an out-of-memory condition.
docstring:
Summary:  
Maps user-space I/O vectors to a bio structure for a given request queue, handling page references and alignment checks.

Parameters:  
q (struct request_queue *): The request queue to which the bio will be associated.  
iter (const struct iov_iter *): The I/O vector iterator containing user-space addresses and lengths.  
gfp_mask (gfp_t): The memory allocation flags for kernel memory allocation.

Returns:  
struct bio *: A pointer to the created bio structure on success, or an error pointer on failure.

Logic:  
The function iterates over the provided I/O vectors, calculating the number of pages required and checking for alignment and overflow errors. It allocates memory for the bio and the page array, retrieves user pages, and adds them to the bio while managing references. If any errors occur during this process, it cleans up allocated resources and returns an appropriate error pointer. Finally, it sets a flag on the bio to indicate that it is user-mapped and returns the bio pointer.

steps.why_it_matters: If the user-space buffer is not aligned to the logical block size of the device, the I/O operation may fail or cause performance issues. The target checks alignment only once at the start, not for each iovec.

judge_vs_vulnerable.rationale: The target implementation omits a consensus step: checking for alignment of the I/O vector data to the logical block size of the request queue. Most independent implementations include this check, while the target performs it only once at the start of the function and does not re-check for each iovec. This could lead to misaligned I/O operations on certain devices.

steps.step: alignment check before adding page to bio
steps.why_it_matters: If the user-space buffer is not aligned to the logical block size of the request queue, the I/O operation may fail or be inefficient. The target does not re-check alignment when adding the page to the bio, which could result in misaligned I/O.

judge_vs_fixed.rationale: The target implementation does not perform a check for the alignment of the I/O vector data to the logical block size of the request queue after the initial calculation of the number of pages. While it checks alignment during the initial loop, it does not re-check alignment when mapping the pages into the bio. A majority of the independent implementations perform this alignment check before adding the page to the bio. This omission could lead to misaligned I/O operations, which may cause performance issues or errors on certain hardware.
